messages:
Jordan (support): hi @here — escalation from Mateo at Acme. Customer on Private/VPC deployment seeing intermittent 429s and spikes of latency after a deploy yesterday. They say it looks like rate limiting + burst exhaustion on their gateway. calling for quick triage.

Mateo (customer): yes. we started getting a flood of 429s around 10:05 UTC. traffic pattern: lots of short-lived clients from a single CIDR (mobile clients). no change in client behavior. we hit their quota? billing alerted but we haven't changed limits. details: private-gw-01 in us-east-1, nginx-ingress v1.6, envoy sidecar for mTLS. logs show repeated 429 with body "rate_limit_exceeded".

Jordan (support): pinging @Alex and @Priya — can you help confirm whether this is gateway-side rate limit or something upstream?

Alex (eng-runtime): thanks. two quick things to validate: 1) are the 429s coming from the customer-managed gateway (NGINX) or from our control-plane token bucket enforcement? 2) are they per-IP or global? Mateo, can you paste a snippet of the 429 response headers and a short log tail?

Mateo (customer): here's a sample response (sanitized):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:05:12 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 167
Request-Id: abcd-1234
Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}
```

Log tail from ingress (time-correlated):
```
10:05:12 GET /v1/generate 10.1.2.45 -> 10.0.1.12 429 "limit reached" route=api/model
10:05:13 GET /v1/generate 10.1.2.46 -> 10.0.1.12 200 "ok" route=api/model
10:05:13 GET /v1/generate 10.1.2.45 -> 10.0.1.12 429 "limit reached" route=api/model
```

Jordan (support): those X-RateLimit headers look like the gateway added them. could be nginx ingress rate-limiting or an envoy local limiter.

Priya (eng-infra): couple of typical private/VPC gotchas we see:
- ingress controller local rate limits set with token-bucket and small burst size; when a bunch of short clients reconnect you see bursts that exhaust the bucket and create transient 429s.
- conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion on busy ephemeral-client patterns (creates 502/503 sometimes, and weird interplay with upstream retry logic).
- Redis-backed global rate-limit service becoming a bottleneck (if they configured an external ratelimit service).

Can you check annotations on the nginx ingress? e.g., `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst`, or envoy config `local_rate_limit` and the external rate limit service (RLS) settings.

Mateo (customer): they use the nginx ingress controller from our helm chart. our ingress has these annotations: `limit-rps: "100"` and `limit-burst: "20"`. we also have an envoy filter with `local_rate_limit` disabled. we don't run RLS.

Alex (eng-runtime): okay that points to nginx token-bucket. two possible mitigations: raise limit-burst (to tolerate simultaneous short-client spikes) and/or switch to per-client (per-ip or per-header key) limiting instead of global. For mobile clients coming from a NATed GW, per-ip won't help — consider rate limit by api-key header.

Sam (eng-sre): also watch the ingress worker concurrency and proxy_buffering settings — small buffers can cause upstream latency and a pile-up of connections making the controller decide to reject. On NGINX ingress, check `worker-connections` and `keepalive` settings.

Jordan (support): Mateo — can you reproduce quickly with a controlled load test? small reproducer will speed fixes. recommended commands:

```
# simple RPS burst with hey
hey -z 10s -q 50 -c 200 -H "Authorization: Bearer <customer-key>" https://private-gw-01.acme.example/v1/generate

# curl loop for a single IP (from a bastion)
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <customer-key>" https://private-gw-01.acme.example/v1/generate; done
```

Mateo (customer): running hey now... seeing 429s spike after ~2s. stack traces show nginx returning the 429s, not our backend.

Alex (eng-runtime): good repro. Suggested immediate mitigation steps (order matters):
1) temporarily increase `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst` to 100, and `limit-rps` to 500 for the route to let current burst drain.
2) add per-key limiting: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-by-key: "$http_authorization"` so tokens are per API key.
3) for long term, move rate-limiting to a Redis-backed RLS with a higher capacity or use our managed rate-limiter in the control plane.

Priya (eng-infra): also check the kube-proxy / conntrack settings if they report client sockets in TIME_WAIT causing port exhaustion. Commands:

```
# on node
ss -s | head
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
# tune ephemeral ports
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
```

If nf_conntrack_max is low relative to clients you get dropped connections and retries that look like bursts.

Sam (eng-sre): addition: inspect the ingress metrics in Prometheus: `nginx_ingress_controller_requests{status=\"429\"}` and `nginx_ingress_controller_limit_requests_total`. Also look at `envoy_local_rate_limit` metrics if enabled.

Mateo (customer): applied the quick change to annotations — increased burst to 120 and limit-rps to 700 for the route. after a minute the 429s dropped to near zero. latency improved. are there any downstream cost/billing implications? our billing spiked because a large number of requests were retried previously.

Jordan (support): we'll coordinate billing. keep evidence (timestamps, request-ids, traces) so billing can consider a one-time credit or reclassification. @Sam, can you open a billing ticket referencing the request-ids?

Sam (eng-sre): will do. please upload the example Request-Id bundles and the hey output. I'll attach Prometheus graphs.

Alex (eng-runtime): follow-ups / long-term recommendations:
- switch from global token-bucket to per-key token buckets (by api-key header) to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- enable graceful degradation: queue-length limiter + prioritized requests for paid tiers.
- set appropriate `X-RateLimit-*` semantics so clients can back off (they had a reset header but it was fractional).
- implement burst-absorbing proxies (small local cache) or jittered retries on client side.
- consider using our Dedicated/private feature that supports configurable autoscaling and built-in rate-limiting hooks.

Priya (eng-infra): config snippets for nginx ingress annotations we recommended:

```
annotations:
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "700"
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "120"
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-by-key: "$http_authorization"
  nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-exempt: ""  # optional: exempt routing for healthchecks
```

If using envoy local_rate_limit filter, set token_bucket like: `fill_rate: 50, max_tokens: 200, tokens_per_fill: 50`. This gives headroom for short spikes.

Mateo (customer): we'll roll the annotations to all clusters and add per-key limiting. any suggestions for testing before prod rollout?

Alex (eng-runtime): yes: test in staging with the same NAT/load shape: simulate many short lived clients from same egress IP vs many unique API keys. Monitor `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `429` metrics. Also test client-side retry jitter: exponential backoff + capped retries.

infra-bot: incident-note created: incident/priv-gw-rateburst-1802500000. Assigning to eng-infra.

Jordan (support): thanks everyone — Mateo can you keep this thread updated after you rollout per-key limits? we'll mark resolved once stable and billing ticket is opened. :thumbsup:

Mateo (customer): per-key rollout done in prod. 24h lookback shows 99.98% success and transient 429s gone. will upload logs and hey traces. thanks team.

Sam (eng-sre): billing ticket filed (BT-1123) referencing request ids, graphs attached. closing loop once customer confirms final reconciliation.

Jordan (support): closing notes for knowledge base: add an article under support/private-vpc-rate-limits summarizing triage checklist: check ingress annotations, conntrack/ephemeral ports, RLS health, promote per-key limiting, short-term burst increases, and repro commands.

Alex (eng-runtime): also add a sample envoy and nginx config snippet to our private deployment recipes.

Mateo (customer): thanks all!
